newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks seen heading lower at open.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks seen heading lower at open.

* Toronto stocks were expected to continue lower at the open on Friday as bank stocks remained soft after Thursday's bank rate hike. * Trading was expected to be quiet ahead of holiday.
Toronto stocks were expected to continue lower at the open on Friday as the banking sector remained soft following the central bank's Thursday rate hike.

"(The market) is probably going south, would be my guess. The bank rate change caught everybody yesterday, (it) probably doesn't have much to do with interest rates at the present time, but it is an indicator," said one trader.
Trading will likely be quiet ahead of Tuesday's Canada Day national holiday, which many will stretch into a long weekend.
Toronto's key 300 Composite Index dropped 61.41 points or nearly one percent yesterday to close at 6453.65.
The Bank of Canada's surprise move to hike short-term interest rates by 25 basis points, the first such hike in more than two years, prompted investors to sell stocks in favor of the dollar.
The trader said gold stocks will continue to be a feature on the negative side as prices languished and the economy showed continued signs of growth.

Revised gross domestic product data out of the United States this morning showed stronger foreign trade pushed the U.S. economy ahead at an even faster clip than previously thought in the first quarter of the year. U.S. GDP for the quarter was revised to 5.9 percent from 5.8 percen.
"The economy doesn't appear to be slowing down in the U.S., which could have a mild negative" effect ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve meeting next week, the trader said.
The markets have widely ruled out a Fed move to hike short-term interest rates at its July 1-2 meeting.
--- STOCKS TO WATCH ---

* Royal Bank of Canada said this morning it would offer C$27.50 a share to acquire all the outstanding common shares of London Insurance Group for a total of C$2.4 billion. London Insurance's majority shareholder, Trilon Financial Corp said it had agreed to tender its 57-percent stake to the offer.
* The union representing striking workers at Inco Ltd's Sudbury division endorsed a deal Thursday afternoon to end the four-week strike.
